quickCheck.question: In a complete robotic control loop, what is the correct chronological sequence of operations?
options: Sense the environment -> Process data with logic -> Command output actuators
Command output actuators -> Sense the environment -> Turn off the power
Process logic -> Command output actuators -> Wire the breadboard
quickCheck.explanation: Robotic systems follow the Sense -> Think -> Act loop: gather sensor data, process decisions in code, and command physical outputs.

quickCheck.question: Which command turns an alert LED connected to digital pin 13 ON when a sensor threshold is triggered?
quickCheck.explanation: digitalWrite(13, HIGH) sends 5V to digital pin 13, illuminating the connected LED.
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: From Lesson 5: digitalWrite(pin, HIGH) applies full 5V power to make an LED illuminate.

steps.title: The Closed-Loop Perception-Action Architecture
steps.markdownContent:
### The Complete Cybernetic Feedback Loop

Robots don't just sense the world—they react to it! This is called the **Perception-Action Loop**:

```
+──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
|                    CLOSED-LOOP ROBOT CONTROLLER                          |
|                                                                          |
|   1. SENSE:  Read hardware input (analogRead(A0) or pulseIn(echoPin))    |
|        │                                                                 |
|        ▼                                                                 |
|   2. THINK:  Compare value against threshold in conditional if/else      |
|        │                                                                 |
|        ▼                                                                 |
|   3. ACT:    Drive actuator pin (digitalWrite(13, HIGH) or tone())       |
|        │                                                                 |
|        ▼                                                                 |
|   4. REPEAT: Loop immediately to maintain real-time responsiveness       |
+──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
```

Every autonomous system—from automatic room nightlights to self-driving cars—runs this loop continuously.

interactiveConfig.question: What is the correct execution sequence inside loop() for an autonomous sensor-driven alarm?
options: Read sensor input -> Evaluate threshold condition -> Command output actuator
Command output actuator -> Compile C++ sketch -> Read sensor input
Unplug USB cable -> Set pin modes -> Measure circuit voltage

questions.question: What happens if you command digitalWrite(13, HIGH) in code without first calling pinMode(13, OUTPUT) in setup()?
options: The pin remains in high-impedance INPUT mode and an attached LED will only glow very faintly or not at all
The microcontroller chip will burn out immediately
The LED blinks at 10,000 Hz automatically
questions.explanation: Without pinMode(13, OUTPUT), the pin remains in high-impedance input mode; writing HIGH merely enables the internal weak pull-up resistor, providing barely enough current to illuminate an LED faintly.
